title: Arise, My Soul, Arise
description: Arise, My Soul, Arise in Tonic Solfa to ST. JOHN (PARISH CHOIR), doh is D: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 5 verses and a piano.
about: Charles Wesley wrote these words. They were printed in the Evangelical Lutheran Hymn-Book (St. Louis, 1927), as hymn 240.

The book printed the words without tunes, marked Hallelujah Metre (6.6.6.6.8.8), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to ST. JOHN (PARISH CHOIR); any other Hallelujah Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: A-rise, my soul, a-rise, Shake off thy guilt-y fears, The bleed-ing Sac-ri-fice In my be-half ap-pears; Be-fore the throne my Sure-ty stands, My name is writ-ten on His hands.

lines: Before the throne my Surety stands,
My name is written on His hands.
His blood atoned for all our race
And sprinkles now the throne of grace.
Forgive him, O forgive, they cry,
Nor let that ransomed sinner die!
His Spirit answers to the blood
And tells me I am born of God.
He owns me for His child,
With confidence I now draw nigh

licence: Public domain: Charles Wesley died in 1788.
credits: Words by Charles Wesley (1707–1788), public domain, as printed in the Evangelical Lutheran Hymn-Book (1927); set to ST. JOHN (PARISH CHOIR) by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
